answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent network can mandate remote attestation from secure hardware enclaves. Nodes must present cryptographic proofs signed by fused silicon keys, anchoring the structural timber of admission. Adversaries incur the verifiable capital cost of buying physical chips encased in onyx resin per identity, preventing a cheap plume of synthetic peers. However, microarchitectural side-channels can leak keys, and reliance on chipmakers centralizes trust.
